equation_request.abstract: We generalize an efficient exact synthesis algorithm for single-qubit unitaries over the Clifford+T gate set which was presented by Kliuchnikov, Maslov and Mosca. Their algorithm takes as input an exactly synthesizable single-qubit unitary–one which can be expressed without error as a product of Clifford and T gates–and outputs a sequence of gates which implements it. The algorithm is optimal in the sense that the length of the sequence, measured by the number of T gates, is smallest possible. In this paper, for each positive even integer $n$ we consider the “Clifford-cyclotomic” gate set consisting of the Clifford group plus a $z$-rotation by $\frac{\pi}{n}$. We present an efficient exact synthesis algorithm which outputs a decomposition using the minimum number of $\frac{\pi}{n}$ $z$-rotations. For the Clifford+T case $n=4$ the group of exactly synthesizable unitaries was shown to be equal to the group of unitaries with entries over the ring $\mathbb{Z}[e^{i\frac{\pi}{n}},1/2]$. We prove that this characterization holds for a handful of other small values of $n$ but the fraction of positive even integers for which it fails to hold is $100\%$.

specification.problem: Exact synthesis of single-qubit unitaries over the Clifford-cyclotomic gate set (Clifford group plus a z-rotation by pi/n, n a positive even integer): given an exactly synthesizable unitary, output a gate sequence using the minimum number of pi/n z-rotations. Also characterize when exactly synthesizable unitaries equal those with entries over Z[e^{i pi/n},1/2].
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level problem statement and ring characterization only. The detailed synthesis algorithm, its proofs, and the list of exceptional n are not in the abstract and are not reconstructed. No measurement or sampling stage exists.

specification.initial_state: Not a state-preparation task; the input is a classical description of U (2x2 matrix with entries in R_n, assumed exactly synthesizable). Circuit acts on an arbitrary single-qubit input.

steps.description: Input classical matrix U and check its entries lie in R_n (necessary condition for exact synthesizability for the cases where the characterization holds).

Iteratively reduce U by multiplying by Clifford gates and one R_z(pi/n) factor per round, following a generalized KMM-style reduction that lowers a size measure of the entries, until reaching a Clifford. Details of the reduction are not given in the abstract.
Invert the recorded reductions to output the gate sequence over G_n with the minimal number of pi/n z-rotations.

specification.measurement: None. The task is a deterministic classical compilation of U into a gate sequence; no quantum measurement is part of the abstract's algorithm.
specification.classical_postprocessing: The whole algorithm is classical: arithmetic over R_n for the reductions, then inverting the recorded reductions to output the gate sequence and counting the pi/n rotations. The abstract gives no further details.
assumptions: The reduction step is a generalization of the Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca approach; its concrete form is assumed, not given in the abstract.
